resumen: The bench press with the bar mounted on guides that only let it move straight up and down. The machine balances the bar, has hooks to rack it at several heights and stops that catch it if you fail, so it is easier to do without a spotter.
ejecucion: Place a flat bench under the bar so it comes down over the middle or lower chest, and set the safety stops so the bar stops just below the point where it touches your chest; check it first with the empty bar.
Lie down so the bar sits over your middle or lower chest, feet on the floor and shoulder blades squeezed together, and grip it slightly wider than your shoulders, wrists straight.
Straighten your arms to lift the bar and rotate it to release it from the hooks.
Lower it under control until it brushes your chest, elbows at about 45-60° from your torso.
Press until your arms are straight, without lifting your back or glutes off the bench.
When you finish, rotate the bar to hook it and make sure it is resting before you let go.
matices: In a study comparing the free-weight and Smith machine bench press, the middle deltoid was more active on the free weight; the abstract does not highlight differences in the anterior deltoid or the pectoralis major. The fixed path removes the work of balancing the bar; in exchange, the bar always follows the same vertical line, even if it is not the one you would follow with a free bar.

fuentes.titulo: A comparison of muscle activation between a Smith machine and free weight bench press
